analysis.title: Implied Thoughts: Equity-Rates correlation reverses sharply: are bonds a hedge again?
key_insights: The 3-month correlation between S&P 500 daily log returns and daily changes in the US 10Y yield hit a 30-year low of -63% on 1 October, while equities and yields were both near 20-year highs. SG says the last comparable configuration was 1999.
The correlation reversed sharply in the past two weeks. On Thursday the US 10Y yield fell almost 20bp while the S&P 500 fell 1.2% and the Nasdaq fell 2.9%.

SG says equities absorbed higher rates because earnings were resilient, but the strongly negative sensitivity to rates left the market in a fragile equilibrium where any further rise in yields was an incremental headwind.

Concerns about the sustainability of the AI boom and wider credit spreads triggered a small equity correction. SG says the move was strong enough to break through the long-gamma resistance that had dampened S&P 500 moves, and implied volatility is now responding more.
The sharp fall in the US 10Y yield suggests duration is again protecting portfolios as risk appetite weakens.
SG reads the correlation reversal together with the end of volatility suppression as an early sign that the dominant market risk is shifting from rates and inflation back to growth and risk appetite.
earnings_insights: SG attributes the equity market's ability to absorb higher bond yields to resilient earnings. No specific EPS or revenue figures are given.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The yield fell as equities sold off, which SG reads as duration providing protection again.

The scatter 'S&P500 implied volatility is finally reacting' plots daily S&P 500 returns since 1 September 2026 against shifts in the 1-month ATM implied vol skew curve (sticky delta), with 22-Oct labelled.

tension_points.bull_case: Bonds are regaining their hedge role. The 10Y yield fell almost 20bp as equities fell, so duration protects again as risk appetite weakens.
tension_points.bear_case: The negative correlation had left the market fragile. Any further rise in yields would be an incremental headwind to equities, and the AI-boom and credit-spread worries behind the correction are still unresolved.
